programmes.name_local: Fondeso - Fondo para el Desarrollo Social de la Ciudad de México
programmes.name_en: Mexico City Social Development Fund (Fondeso) microcredit
programmes.funder: Fondo para el Desarrollo Social de la Ciudad de México (Fondeso), Gobierno de la Ciudad de México
programmes.amount_note: Micro and small business credit at preferential rates for Mexico City residents, with tiers historically from around MXN 5,000 up to about MXN 200,000 depending on the product and the business's track record.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling applications through Fondeso modules across Mexico City, subject to annual budget.
programmes.reopen_note: Fondeso's product line and ceilings are reset each budget year by the Mexico City government; check fondeso.cdmx.gob.mx for the current tiers.

procedure_steps.detail: Attend a Fondeso module or apply online.
Complete the required financial education training.
Submit the application with proof of the business activity.
Approval and disbursement with a repayment schedule.

eligibility.other_note: Mexico City residents running or starting a micro or small business; aimed at financial inclusion rather than technology startups.

programmes.name_local: Programa de Estímulos a la Innovación (PEI)
programmes.funder: Consejo Nacional de Humanidades, Ciencias y Tecnologías (Conahcyt, formerly CONACYT), Mexico
programmes.amount_note: Provided non-reimbursable support for company R&D projects (INNOVAPYME, INNOVATEC and PROINNOVA modalities), with awards commonly in the millions of Mexican pesos and mandatory company counterpart funding.
programmes.deadline_note: The PEI was discontinued after the 2019 federal budget as part of the restructuring of CONACYT into Conahcyt.
programmes.reopen_note: Not reinstated. Conahcyt's current instruments emphasise national strategic projects (Pronaces / Pronaii) and public research rather than direct company R&D subsidies. Mexican companies seeking R&D co-funding now generally rely on state programmes, development banking (NAFIN, Bancomext) and private capital. Kept here because founders still search for the PEI.

eligibility.other_note: Was open to Mexican companies in the RENIECYT register, in three modalities depending on company size and academic collaboration.

programmes.funder: Instituto Nacional del Emprendedor (INADEM), Secretaría de Economía, Mexico
programmes.amount_note: Historically Mexico's main SME and startup grant vehicle, co-financing projects across incubation, acceleration, technology adoption and scaling, with award sizes set per convocatoria.
programmes.deadline_note: INADEM was abolished and the Fondo Nacional Emprendedor discontinued from the 2019 federal budget. No further convocatorias have been issued.
programmes.reopen_note: Permanently discontinued as a federal grant vehicle, but retained here because it remains the reference point Mexican founders search for. Federal support has shifted to credit through Nacional Financiera (NAFIN), the Programa de Microcréditos para el Bienestar and state-level and municipal programmes (for example Fondeso in Mexico City), rather than a national startup grant fund. As of August 2026 no successor national startup grant fund has been created.

procedure_steps.detail: Not applicable - discontinued. Mexican founders should look to NAFIN credit lines, state economic development secretariats and CDMX Fondeso.

eligibility.other_note: Was open to Mexican MSMEs and entrepreneurs through annual convocatorias.

programmes.funder: Secretaría de Economía with Fondo de Fondos (Corporación Mexicana de Inversiones de Capital)
programmes.amount_note: Co-investment through the Fondo de Fondos: up to 6 million pesos for seed capital and up to 20 million pesos for venture/growth capital. The Fondo de Fondos covers up to 50% of an investment round; private institutional funds must cover the remainder. Investment periods of 5-7 years with 10-12 year exit horizons.
programmes.deadline_note: 'Convocatoria cerrada el 30 de abril del 2026' — the most recent call closed on 30 April 2026. The programme is presented as an ongoing instrument of Plan México; check the microsite for the next call.

procedure_steps.detail: Verify that the company is formally incorporated in Mexico and operates in a Plan México strategic sector.
Register through the electronic form on the programme microsite while a call is open.
Selected companies are matched with private institutional funds; Fondo de Fondos co-invests up to 50% of the round via equity or convertible instruments (SAFEs, notas convertibles).

documents_required.doc: Electronic registration form on the microsite
Acta constitutiva / proof of formal incorporation in Mexico

eligibility.other_note: Mexican companies 'formalmente constituidas', operating in Plan México strategic sectors (AI, semiconductors, clean energy, biotech, agri-innovation, advanced manufacturing, telecommunications, security tech, mobility, cybersecurity), at early, growth or consolidation stage, and able to receive private capital through equity or convertible instruments.

programmes.source_snippet: Programa que apoya proyectos ciudadanos de innovación y de tecnologías avanzadas ... Convocatoria cerrada el 30 de abril del 2026.

programmes.name_en: Nacional Financiera — business financing for MSMEs (guaranteed bank credit)
programmes.amount_note: 'Hasta 20 mdp' (up to 20 million pesos), term 'Hasta 5 años', rate 'Anual conforme al destino'. Nafin guarantees/funds the credit; the participating commercial bank sets the final rate and authorises the loan.
programmes.deadline_note: Continuous — a standing credit programme delivered through 15+ participating banks (BBVA, Citibanamex, HSBC, Banorte and others), not a call.

procedure_steps.detail: Confirm you meet the requirements (formal business, favourable credit bureau history, minimum two years of operation, sufficient cash flow).
Contact one of the participating banks listed by Nafin.
The bank evaluates creditworthiness and authorises the loan directly.

documents_required.doc: Documentation requested by the participating bank
Evidence of at least two years of business operation

eligibility.other_note: 'Para las Micro, Pequeñas y Medianas Empresas mexicanas de los sectores industria, comercio y servicios'. Requires a favourable credit bureau history and a minimum of two years of operation — so it is not available to pre-revenue startups.

programmes.source_snippet: Para las Micro, Pequeñas y Medianas Empresas mexicanas de los sectores industria, comercio y servicios ... Hasta 20 mdp ... Hasta 5 años.
